title: Super Supportive

source.nextStart: It was nearly eleven when Alden arrived in front of the consulate building.
source.continuationNote: Late-night arrival, gate conversation, shoes off, Victor released, invitation to ride elevators. Stop before their tour.

completed.end: Hannah agrees to ask about the shrapnel and admires Alden’s scar; he feels heard. The cause of his parents’ deaths is not yet explained.
Hannah explains the bubble and the pursuit to the empty building. Alden learns that even his rescuer does not fully understand her powers.
Hannah admits counting the wrong floor. Alden cries and shouts for everyone to leave; Hannah goes while Amanda approaches, the opposite of what he wanted.
Alden finishes his System homework but cannot sleep in the noisy apartment.
Alden tests the response time; Connie reaches and comforts him in eight seconds. The ninety-second question remains unresolved.
Alden finds Hannah’s note, calls, and learns she listed him as a priority contact. He chooses audio only; the System forwards his call before Hannah answers.
At Cly’s farewell brunch Hannah receives Alden’s call, confirms approximately ninety seconds, and is rattled by his abrupt goodbye. The call notification flashes again and she answers immediately.
Alden offers his explanation for his parents’ deaths and asks Hannah to tell Thomas. Hannah promises a summer visit and teleport, then learns how costly it will be. School break is in three weeks.
Five years later, Alden and friends trade jokes on their way to alien school; he privately asks to replay his last three voicemails.

Alden replays Hannah’s summons message and Cly’s two updates. Hannah has been missing six months; her friends propose a funeral on her birthday. Alden switches off the System without answering the teleport invitation. Her death is not confirmed.

After replaying the messages, Alden sees the repaired city and recalls Hannah’s changed heroic motto. At eleven he found it sad; now he considers Skiff’s emotional burden and why complementary support could change a fight. Hannah’s absence remains unresolved.

Jeremy brings Alden back to the train stop. Friends tease one another about being funny, mean and nice. Jeremy identifies Alden’s persistent heroic dream beneath his sensible college planning; Alden is embarrassed and Boe is impressed.

Alden brings Gorgon coconut-milk hot chocolate and spicy food. Gorgon challenges his motives. Alden admits hoping for friendship and future System advice, learns that magical restraints prevent secret information, and quietly explains that a friend thought his selection chances might be better than normal. He admits having a specific dream.

Alden recalls Hannah’s uncertain clue about remaining conscious in her bubble. After Gorgon lists his limited public services, Alden promises to keep bringing food. Gorgon strains to explain he is not vegan but cannot name food or make requests. Alden suspects a punitive restriction and proposes trial and error; the reason remains unknown.

After Gorgon’s embarrassing assessment of classmates, Alden spends history class listing affordable food tests. At lunch he explains Gorgon cannot request food or answer a question about insects; Boe now wants to try feeding him too.

Lunch speculation about blood and crickets remains only speculation. In wordchaining Alden hears Jeremy mistakenly offer his brain, then recognizes that his own correct words lack focus. He lets himself imagine being selected despite the odds.
Alden recognizes how much Hannah mattered to him, reassures Jeremy without sharing his grief, and stays for writing class to avoid a lonely home. When everyone leaves he returns to Gorgon’s desk.
Alden learns Gorgon has no room, asks about food and loneliness, and realizes that unwanted attention is cruel because Gorgon cannot escape cameras. He has not yet proposed crickets.

Alden proposes live crickets and asks whether unusual food would offend. He notices raw skin under Gorgon’s bindings. Gorgon appreciates his gifts but calls the earlier disclosure a costly moment of melancholy, not a problem for Alden to solve. No food test has occurred; the cost is unexplained.

Alden playfully insists on friendship. His thirty live crickets go uneaten, but Gorgon privately smiles and releases them into the lobby plants. Weeks later they still chirp; Alden continues bringing one vegetarian and one meat dish without success. The butcher-shop discussion has not begun.

In the butcher shop Boe questions whether Alden’s food mission avoids Hannah’s funeral. Alden says he probably will not attend because others knew her better. Jeremy urges him to go for his own sake. Boe breaks the painful silence with an absurd prison-break/Chicago-doom joke, gets Jeremy’s glare, and recommends tongue tacos that Alden can eat if Gorgon refuses. No attendance decision or meal outcome.

In wordchain class Alden practices the luck request his mother taught him and remembers Hannah’s bubble. He interrupts self-blame, knows he must return Hannah’s friend’s call, and thinks about the funeral ten days away. He believes Hannah is almost certainly gone but has no confirmation. Her sincere wish to make her life matter does not comfort him. No phone call or funeral decision occurs.

Alden returns to Connie’s California note. Fear of being taken into care resurfaces; he reasons that money and approaching sixteen may protect his independence. Crushed bread, an unpaid electric bill, dirty cups and unfamiliar tiger-striped shorts defeat his attempts to stay calm. Stops before Victor arrives; no phone call or funeral decision.

Victor arrives and Alden welcomes the distraction. Cat food is missing despite a search of cupboards, drawers, fridge and trash. He suspects Connie or the unknown owner of the tiger shorts without evidence. Two messages receive no reply; he gives Victor a small piece of bologna. After showering he dries his hair and tries not to judge Connie. No phone call or funeral decision.

Alden reaches Clytem Zhao’s voicemail, apologizes for his late reply and accepts the funeral invitation if transport is not too much trouble. Decision made, he dresses, takes his pillow and invites Victor to get tuna and meet someone, joking about demons. They have not reached Gorgon yet.

defaults.scope: Intimate character drama. Preserve quiet episodes and substantial local payoffs. Occasional source-supported perspective shifts welcomed.
defaults.choices: Four local observation or conversational choices; preserve canonical events.
defaults.language: Simplified Mandarin, interlinear chunks, reviewed pinyin, cached Mandarin audio.
defaults.openingArt: Each opening depicts an episode-specific event, location, action and composition. Preserve approved character identity while experimenting with a distinct art medium each episode. Identity references must not cause repeated scenery.

continuity: Hannah remains missing, not confirmed dead.
Gorgon’s food restrictions remain unresolved. No proposed food test has been carried out.
Alden has no confirmed selection or powers; the effect of his wordchain is uncertain.
